name: Belt trick
description: An infinite lattice of cubes joined by six ribbons, spinning through 720 degrees and untangling itself - the Dirac belt trick. The ribbons never break because the rotation is applied as a spinor, so a full double turn returns to the identity.

cycle.description: Seconds for one full 720-degree untangle. Shorter reads as frantic; the geometry needs time to be legible.

orbit.description: Camera orbit speed around the lattice.

distance.description: Camera distance. Further back shows more cells of the lattice.

steps.description: March steps. The twist makes this field far from a true distance function, so it needs a lot of them.

fog.description: Depth haze. This is what keeps the infinite lattice from reading as visual noise.

tint.description: Blend the per-axis ribbon colours toward the project palette. The cube faces stay keyed so the rotation remains readable.
